what: The score combines exact insertion-distance increase, a depot-radius credit, a capacity-fill penalty, and a short compatible-neighbor penalty. The slot is therefore selected by cheapest insertion, while customer priority favors remote customers that merge economically, leave usable residual capacity, and have a nearby customer that can still fit. Each call uses O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) time and O(1) extra space.
why: Farthest-customer route seeding benefits from continuing within the same remote spatial region instead of immediately consuming capacity with cheap near-depot insertions. The radial credit approximates route-merging savings, while the compatible-neighbor term promotes compact clusters that intra-route 2-opt can subsequently organize. The load-dependent fill penalty is especially relevant when demands are large relative to capacity: it discourages choices that strand unusable capacity, using only lightweight aggregate and largest-fitting-demand statistics rather than solving knapsack. The coefficients are scale-normalized but heuristic; unusual demand distributions, non-clustered geometry, or different GRASP alpha values may warrant tuning, and no performance improvement is claimed without evaluation.
